gaps.note: Commercial break edit cuts between Kevin's exit and Meagan's response.

stage_a.note: Delivers the pitch with a smile and an engaging, positive tone throughout.
Shows strong engagement and excitement when introducing her floral solution.
Smiles warmly and addresses the panel directly with a friendly, approachable demeanor.

venture.description: Scented, long-lasting artificial floral bouquets made from recycled and sustainable materials.
venture.note: The product is positioned as an alternative to real flowers for gifts and weddings.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Introduces herself, asks for investment, explains the problem with real flowers dying, and presents her sustainable floral solution.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains she has gifts for each of the investors and begins handing them out.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Thanks the founder and admires the custom wooden map art piece he received.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains the locations depicted on the wooden map art piece for Robert.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Makes a loud sniffing noise while examining the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Hands Lori one of the custom flower bouquets.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Thanks the founder and compliments the beauty of the bouquet.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Hands Kevin a bridal bouquet and a matching boutonniere, explaining the items.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Smells the bouquet and correctly identifies the black raspberry scent.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Comments on how good the bouquet smells.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Hands Barbara a spring-themed bouquet.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Expresses love for the spring colors of her bouquet.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Hands Daymond a box containing lapels for his jacket.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Reacts positively to receiving the lapels.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: Asks to confirm that the items Daymond received are lapels.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jokes with Mark that his bouquet has real money in it and he must return it if there is no deal.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: Examines the bouquet made of real money and jokes that he is going to spend it.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks the founder if she individually makes the bouquets herself.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains that she used to make them but demand grew too high, so she now uses two manufacturers.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: Remarks that needing manufacturers is a good sign.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks the female investors how they would feel receiving fake flowers instead of real ones from a man.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Begins to react to the question but is interrupted.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks the founder if she wants an honest answer to Robert's question.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees to hear the honest answer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: States that giving fake flowers shows a lack of sensitivity and she would rather have real ones.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Agrees that she would be insulted and wants to feel precious like a real flower.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Argues that her customers feel differently, preferring a lasting gift over expensive real flowers that quickly end up in the garbage.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: Challenges her to prove the other investors wrong by asking what her sales are.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States that her lifetime sales are 2.8 million dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Expresses amazement at the sales figure.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Adds that the business has only been open for a year and a half.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Congratulates the founder on her success.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Continues explaining that all sales are direct to consumer through their website.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks what the selling price is for a bundle.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Answers that a bridal bouquet sells for about $59.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks how she came to start this business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains she saw wood flowers on Shark Tank, tried making them, and wouldn't have had the idea without the show.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Points out that there is a lot of competition and questions if nobody else has a bouquet.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Clarifies that while people buy individual flowers for crafting on Etsy, nobody else sells complete bouquets online for gifts.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asserts that they are not used heavily in the wedding industry because people prefer live flowers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Counters that the industry relies on commissions, but she recently started weddings and made $25k from them just yesterday.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: Asks what caused the sudden $100k spike in sales the previous day.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains they usually hold back marketing due to production, but yesterday spent $4k on an ad which generated $90k.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: Asks what a typical day in sales was prior to that ad spend.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Answers that a typical day was anywhere from 6,000 to 13,000 dollars.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: Praises her for creating another $90k in sales and killing it.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: Asks how much of her own money is invested in the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Answers that she has put in about $700.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Elaborates that a business partner invested when she was about to be homeless, paying her rent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks how much equity she sold to that partner and for how much money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains he put in $3,000 upfront and paid her rent for a year in exchange for 25%.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks to confirm that the partner got 25% for $3,000 and paying rent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms the terms.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks if she has taken on any other investors.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains that she needed another investment for inventory and found a local firm that gave $30k for 50% split between two guys.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Points out that this means 50% of the equity is gone.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: Notes that this leaves only 25% ownership for the founder.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Summarizes that she sold 75% of her business for roughly $35,000.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Concedes that it was hard times and agrees with the summary.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Criticizes her for giving away her equity, defeating the purpose of starting a business.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: States he would want 30% but she has no equity to give, making her just an employee, so he is out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Addresses the panel's concern about her equity, reiterating her ask of $400k for 10%.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Reiterates his challenge of where the stock would come from if he wanted 30%.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains that equity would come from equal shares, and she wants to buy out her current tech investors.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks if the plan is to use a Shark's money to buy out the current investors.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms that the equity could be used differently and the current investors are open to being bought out.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Argues she should retain more equity in a small business, notes she doesn't control it, and exits.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: States she spends a lot on flowers but doesn't understand this product, so it's not right for her, and exits.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: Praises her work but says the floral business is not his area of expertise, and exits.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Claims she sees these types of flowers readily available everywhere.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Disagrees, arguing there is no real competition because nobody else offers full bouquets online.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Compliments her job but decides it's not the right investment for her, and exits.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Reiterates that investing is impossible without diluting her to an employee.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Defends herself by stating she is doing a great job and is number one in her space.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: States he is going to make an offer of $400,000 for 25%.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Explains his concerns about equity but wants to buy out the other partners eventually, reiterating his offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Counters the offer, proposing $400k for 20% to avoid wiping herself out and to make all partners equal.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Clarifies if the 20% would come equally from all four current partners.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms that the equity will come from all partners equally.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Asks Daymond if they have a deal.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Agrees to the counter-offer terms.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Excitedly accepts the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Hugs Daymond and repeatedly thanks him.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Thanks the founder in return while hugging.

turns.speaker: S6
turns.summary: Congratulates the founder on getting a deal.

decisions.note: Thinks she gave away too much equity and would end up just an employee if he took the 30% he would want.
Believes she doesn't control the business and gave away too much equity for a small business.
Does not understand or like the product personally, prefers real flowers.
The floral/craft business is not his area of expertise.
Feels the product is too readily available and not unique enough for her to invest.
Willing to invest despite the equity structure, wants to eventually buy out the other partners.
Wants to keep dilution equal among the 5 partners.

record.notes: Commercial break edit cuts between Kevin's exit and Meagan's response.
